subject: general
question: After removing the carbon deposit on the cylinder head, which of the following is used to clean the cylinder head?
solution:
The correct answer is __Cleaning solvent.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cleaning solvent__ is specifically designed to clean engine parts.
 
• It is effective in removing oil, grease, and other residues from the surface of the cylinder head.
 
• Using a cleaning solvent ensures thorough cleaning without damaging the metal components.
 
• It helps in maintaining engine efficiency and performance after servicing.
 
• Cleaning solvents are non-corrosive and safe to use for mechanical parts.
 
• They evaporate quickly, leaving the surface clean and residue-free.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Diesel:**

 
 
• Diesel can sometimes be used for cleaning, but it is less effective compared to specialized cleaning solvents.
 
• It may leave an oily residue on the surface.
 
 
 
• **Kerosene:**
 
 
• Kerosene can act as a cleaning agent but is not ideal for removing stubborn carbon deposits.
 
• It may not evaporate as quickly as a cleaning solvent, leaving behind residues.
 
 
 
• **Lub Oil:**
 
 
• Lubricating oil is not a cleaning agent and is used for reducing friction in engine parts.
 
• Using it as a cleaning agent can lead to ineffective cleaning and contamination.
